question: Within the accepted 124M candidate's own checkpoint and residual frame, do the next production c_fc and c_proj optimizer moves destructively interfere, cooperate, or produce approximately additive finite-CE effects?

predecessor.repair_scope: Only gradient/context replay identity changed. All data seeds, finite-CE windows, thresholds, and structural authorization remain frozen.

protocol.gradient_clipping: Apply the production global clip over model.product_fht_clip_parameters before masking non-target gradients.
protocol.update_extraction: Compute one production backward pass, snapshot the clipped c_fc/c_proj gradients and functional contexts, restore the exact custom module and optimizer states before each c_fc-only, c_proj-only, and joint replay, and require joint deltas to match singleton deltas at absolute tolerance 1e-7.
protocol.scoring: Apply extracted materialized deltas to the untouched checkpoint and restore after every fixed-window forward.

decision_rule.destructive: The normalized finite interaction is at least +0.25 on both validation windows.
decision_rule.cooperative: The normalized finite interaction is at most -0.10 on both validation windows.
decision_rule.additive: The absolute normalized finite interaction is at most 0.10 on both validation windows.
decision_rule.structural_action: A destructive result authorizes a joint block-output metric chart. An additive but non-helpful joint step instead directs work to the individual prospective directions. No result directly authorizes HyperConnection or a learned residual topology.

execution.monitoring: direct foreground polling only; no watchdog, callback, queue worker, or heartbeat

authorization: This plan authorizes only the zero-persistent-update diagnostic. It does not authorize a training run, a larger rung, HyperConnection, or any residual-topology change.
